subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the SSRF/proxy bypass helpers remain owner-scoped private helpers, or should maintainers approve exposing them through a public Plugin SDK contract to repair the package lazy-load regression?
rationale: The import-only patch cannot work because the public subpath does not export the helper, and adding that export is a security-sensitive SDK boundary choice rather than a mechanical PR repair.

options.title: Preserve owner-scoped private access
options.body: Fix the packaged Browser/Ollama lazy-load path through the existing private owner-scoped resolver or staging mechanism, keeping the helpers out of public Plugin SDK exports.

options.title: Approve public SDK promotion
options.body: Land a broader SDK/security-boundary change only with explicit docs, guardrails, contract tests, release-note context, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Choose a canonical replacement
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers pick the canonical issue or another replacement PR as the repair path for the same regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve owner-scoped private access
recommendation.body: Fix the packaged Browser/Ollama lazy-load path through the existing private owner-scoped resolver or staging mechanism, keeping the helpers out of public Plugin SDK exports.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is package/SDK boundary direction, and this owner history includes private SDK packaging hardening and adjacent private helper boundary work.
